entries.title: Basic Classes
entries.subtitle: The basic classes establish the crew's first division of labor.
entries.summary: Presents the four level-4 basic classes described by the manuscript.
body: Basic classes have a stated maximum level of 4 and provide the broad starting roles from which most crew members enter play.

groups.title: Engineer
groups.summary: Repairs, maintains, modifies, and sometimes sabotages systems; generally less capable in direct combat.

groups.title: Medic
groups.summary: Treats injuries, disease, poison, and crisis casualties; generally less capable in heavy physical tasks.

groups.title: Scientist
groups.summary: Conducts research, analysis, laboratory work, and technical interpretation; may struggle in social situations.

groups.title: Security Officer
groups.summary: Handles weapons, combat, tactical planning, area security, intimidation, and team defense; lacks the technical depth of specialist engineers.

editorialNotes: The source alternates between 'Security officer' and title case. The wiki standardizes the display name as Security Officer.

entries.title: Basic Class Talents
entries.subtitle: Talents provide bonuses, permissions, rerolls, recovery effects, and role-specific advantages.
entries.summary: Converts the seven listed talents for each basic class into searchable groups.
body: A character chooses one Talent at creation and may select additional Talents when gaining levels, subject to class and campaign limits.

talents.name: Quick Fix
talents.effect: Roll an additional die during repair work and retain the best applicable result.

talents.name: MacGyver
talents.effect: Perform improvised repairs when proper replacement materials are unavailable.

talents.name: Tech Wizard
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving technology or complex systems.

talents.name: Demolition Expert
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Strength rolls involving deliberate destruction or sabotage of systems.

talents.name: Tinkerer
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving modification or improvement of existing systems.

talents.name: Gadgeteer
talents.effect: Create original gadgets or devices through technical skill and improvisation.

talents.name: Backup Plan
talents.effect: Receive a second attempt after an initial system-related failure.

talents.name: First Aid
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Agility rolls for medical treatment. A crew member reduced to 0 or fewer stat points may be stabilized if treated within one turn; further damage still kills them.

talents.name: Trauma Specialist
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls for complex treatment; a successful treatment restores 1d6 lost stat points.

talents.name: Healing Hands
talents.effect: Restore 1 lost stat point to a target crew member.

talents.name: Poison Resistance
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Strength rolls involving toxins or poisons affecting the Medic or nearby crew.

talents.name: Diagnostician
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls for diagnosis and restore 1 stat point on a successful treatment.

talents.name: Medical Expert
talents.effect: Gain +1 on rolls involving medicine and medical matters.

talents.name: Emergency Response
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Agility rolls during crisis treatment; injured crew recover 1 stat point for two turns while the Medic takes no other action.

talents.name: Research Prodigy
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving scientific study.

talents.name: Analytical Mind
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving data analysis.

talents.name: Creative Thinker
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving creative problem-solving.

talents.name: Scientific Communication
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Charisma rolls involving presentation of scientific findings.

talents.name: Laboratory Technician
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Agility rolls involving laboratory work.

talents.name: Field Researcher
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Agility rolls involving field research.

talents.name: Scientific Leadership
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Charisma rolls involving leadership of researchers.

talents.name: Combat Training
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Strength rolls involving physical combat.

talents.name: Quick Reflexes
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Agility rolls involving dodging and evasion.

talents.name: Tactical Thinking
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving combat strategy and planning.

talents.name: Weapons Expert
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Strength rolls involving weapon use.

talents.name: Security Specialist
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Intelligence rolls involving security measures.

talents.name: Intimidation
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Charisma rolls involving intimidation, persuasion, or negotiation through authority.

talents.name: Leadership
talents.effect: Gain +2 on Charisma rolls involving command and team leadership.

editorialNotes: Several medical effects use 'lost stat points' as a unified injury resource. The exact relationship between attribute loss, health, stabilization, and death remains to be normalized in the damage chapter.

entries.title: Advanced Classes
entries.subtitle: Advanced roles concentrate command, maintenance, and navigation power at the cost of sharper failure consequences.
entries.summary: Presents the Captain, Mechanic, and Navigator, each with a stated maximum level of 6.
body: Advanced classes have a stated maximum level of 6 and offer talents that can strongly affect the whole crew or submarine.

groups.title: Captain
groups.summary: Leads the vessel, maintains order, manages resources, and controls crew-wide responses.

groups.title: Mechanic
groups.summary: Specializes in keeping the submarine functional, draining flooded spaces, modifying systems, and salvaging usable material.

groups.title: Navigator
groups.summary: Plans routes, controls movement, manages communications, leads dives, predicts currents, and locates salvage.

editorialNotes: The source refers to both 'Mechanic' and 'Mechanics'. The singular class name is used here.

entries.title: Advanced Class Talents
entries.subtitle: Powerful specialist abilities often consume Supply, operate once per route or mission, and punish failure.
entries.summary: Converts the Captain, Mechanic, and Navigator talent lists while preserving stated costs and drawbacks.
body: Advanced talents commonly affect multiple crew members, the submarine, event cards, route length, or major emergencies. Many have explicit limits such as once per mission or once before reaching the next station.

talents.name: Leadership
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to grant the crew +2 to stats for one round. A failed roll imposes -2 for one round and gives the Captain 1 Lost Sanity.

talents.name: Crisis Management
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply and make an Intelligence roll to discard an event card; the talent grants a temporary +4 Intelligence. Failure imposes -2 Intelligence for the mission and 1 Lost Sanity.

talents.name: Resource Management
talents.effect: Grant the crew +1 Strength and Agility for one round. Failure imposes -2 Strength and Agility until reaching a station.

talents.name: People Person
talents.effect: Gain a temporary +5 for negotiation or persuasion. Failure imposes -5 for the negotiation and gives 1 Lost Sanity.

talents.name: Strategic Planning
talents.effect: Before drawing events, gain +6 Agility for one event. Failure imposes -6 Agility for that event.

talents.name: Decision Making
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +3 Strength for one round. Failure imposes -3 Strength for one round.

talents.name: Emotional Control
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +4 Intelligence and remove crew Lost Sanity. Failure imposes -5 Intelligence until reaching a station and instead gives each crew member Lost Sanity.

talents.name: Quick Fixes
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +2 Agility for one round while fixing a small ship problem. Failure imposes -2 Agility for one round.

talents.name: Trick Repair Work
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +4 Strength for one round while repairing a major problem. Failure imposes -4 Strength for one round.

talents.name: Customization
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to grant the submarine +3 Defense for one round. Failure instead imposes -3 Defense for one round.

talents.name: Scrap King
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +5 Strength and Agility for one salvage round. Failure imposes -5 to both for one round.

talents.name: Innovative Thinking
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +6 Intelligence for an improvised solution. The manuscript's failure penalty requires later clarification.

talents.name: Uncommon Expertise
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to gain +5 Intelligence for troubleshooting and repairs for one round. Failure imposes -5 Strength and Agility for one round.

talents.name: Emergency Pump
talents.effect: Spend 1 Supply to grant the submarine +2 Agility for one round through emergency drainage. Failure instead imposes -2 Agility for one round.

talents.name: Navigation Expert
talents.effect: Gain +3 Intelligence for route calculation and reduce required travel events. Usable once before the next station.

talents.name: Quick Thinker
talents.effect: Roll twice and keep the better result for one crisis roll. Usable once before the next station.

talents.name: Mapmaker
talents.effect: Draw two event cards and choose which result to resolve. Usable once per mission.

talents.name: Deep Sea Diver
talents.effect: Roll twice and keep the better result for underwater exploration. Usable once before the next station.

talents.name: Deep Sea Weather Watcher
talents.effect: Roll twice and keep the better result when moving the submarine. Usable once per mission.

talents.name: Distress Signal Expert
talents.effect: Roll twice and keep the better result for vessel communications, then suffer -1 Intelligence until the next station.

talents.name: Salvage Hunter
talents.effect: Roll twice and keep the better result for salvage operations. Usable once before the next station.

editorialNotes: Some source entries use an attribute that does not match the described action, and one Mechanic failure clause is incomplete. These are retained as editorial warnings rather than silently corrected.
